subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Beliefs and teachings: The nature of Allah and key Muslim beliefs
Beliefs and teachings: Risalah, angels, holy books, Al-Qadr and Akhirah
Practices: The Five Pillars and the Ten Obligatory Acts
Practices: Rituals of worship, jihad and festivals

questions.q: What does the Islamic concept of Tawhid mean?
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of Allah, the most central belief in Islam.

questions.q: In Shia Islam, which of the five roots (Usul ad-Din) refers to the justice of God?
questions.explain: Adalat is the belief in the divine justice of Allah, one of the five roots of Shia Islam.

questions.q: Which angel is believed to have revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered the Qur'an to Muhammad over 23 years.

questions.q: According to Islam, which holy book was revealed to the prophet Musa (Moses)?
questions.explain: The Tawrat (Torah) is the scripture Muslims believe was given by Allah to Musa.

questions.q: What does the Islamic belief of Al-Qadr refer to?
questions.explain: Al-Qadr is the belief that Allah has decreed and has knowledge of everything that happens.

questions.q: What percentage of a Muslim's surplus wealth is normally given each year as Zakah?
questions.explain: Zakah requires Muslims to give 2.5% of their surplus wealth to those in need.

questions.q: In Shia Islam, what percentage of surplus income is paid as Khums?
questions.explain: Khums, one of the Ten Obligatory Acts, is a payment of 20% of surplus income in Shia Islam.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims observe the fast of Sawm?
questions.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fast observed from dawn to sunset throughout the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: Why is shirk considered the greatest sin in Islam?
options: It associates partners with Allah, denying Tawhid
It refers to failing to give Zakah
questions.explain: Shirk directly contradicts Tawhid, the belief in the absolute oneness of Allah.

questions.q: The Six Beliefs (including Tawhid, angels and predestination) are most closely associated with which tradition?
questions.explain: The Six Beliefs form the core articles of faith held by Sunni Muslims.

questions.q: Muhammad is described as the 'Seal of the Prophets'. What does this mean?
options: He is the final prophet sent by Allah
questions.explain: As the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad is believed to be the last messenger, completing Allah's revelation.

questions.q: How might belief in Akhirah influence a Muslim's daily behaviour?
options: They act morally, knowing they will be judged on the Day of Judgement
They ignore the teachings of the Qur'an
questions.explain: Belief in life after death and judgement motivates Muslims to live righteously to attain Paradise (Jannah).

questions.q: Why is the Shahadah regarded as the foundation of a Muslim's faith?
options: Sincerely reciting it declares belief in Allah and Muhammad as his messenger
It is a tax paid to the poor
It is a journey made to Makkah
It requires fasting for a month
questions.explain: The Shahadah is the declaration of faith that expresses Tawhid and prophethood, the basis of being a Muslim.

questions.q: The Ten Obligatory Acts, which include Khums and Jihad, belong to which tradition?
options: Both equally as the Five Pillars
questions.explain: Shia Muslims follow the Ten Obligatory Acts, whereas Sunni Muslims emphasise the Five Pillars.

questions.q: What does the term 'greater jihad' refer to in Islam?
options: The personal inner struggle to be a good Muslim
The giving of alms to the poor
questions.explain: Greater jihad is the inner spiritual struggle to follow Allah and resist temptation.

questions.q: What event does the festival of Id-ul-Adha commemorate?
options: Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah
The first revelation of the Qur'an
The end of the fast of Ramadan
The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha, the festival of sacrifice, marks Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son at Allah's command.

questions.q: A Muslim is too ill to fast during Ramadan. According to Islamic teaching, what should they normally do?
options: Make up the missed fasts later or feed the poor
questions.explain: The ill and other exempt groups can make up the fast when able, or provide food to those in need.

questions.q: A Muslim carefully washes their hands, face, arms and feet before an act. Which pillar are they preparing to perform?
questions.explain: This ritual washing is wudu, the purification performed before the prayer (Salah).

questions.q: A male pilgrim in Makkah is wearing two plain white unstitched sheets of cloth. What state is he in?
questions.explain: Ihram is the state of purity and the simple white dress worn by pilgrims performing Hajj.

questions.q: A Muslim who firmly believes in Al-Qadr experiences an unexpected hardship. How are they most likely to respond?
options: By accepting it as part of Allah's will and plan
By concluding that Allah does not exist
questions.explain: Belief in predestination leads Muslims to trust that events occur within Allah's knowledge and decree.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE Religious Studies specification; Component 2: A Study of Islam
